findings.claim: Full sum/dot begins at Competition.posZero. A suffix-only version requires its initial raw accumulator to satisfy P; arbitrary native-NaN seeds are insufficient.
findings.action: Quantify the full original fold, or require P(seed) and matching native seed.

findings.claim: Screen raw original sum values, and both raw A/B reads for each dot k. Products and accumulators are allowed to become NaN, but must remain in P.
findings.action: Use canonical-image closure rather than an assertion that all intermediates are nonNaN. The predicate must allow Inf; isFinite=true or exp!=255 is a safe rejection but would miss the intended nonfinite opportunity. Even all-finite dot inputs can form opposite infinite rounded products.

findings.claim: BMM scanning must cover A[(b*m+i)*n+k] and B[(b*n+k)*p+j], not a contiguous B slice or all indices in a wrong packed lane.
findings.counterexample: batch=1,m=1,n=2,p=2,A=[1,1],B=[0,0,0x7fc00001,1],j=0. Correct B reads [0,2], wrong contiguous reads [0,1]. Raw dot is 0x7fc00001.
findings.action: Prove scanner Boolean true implies all actual total reads are nonNaN for that output and lane.

findings.claim: Out-of-bounds total reads are posZero, including generic dot helper cases. Unused storage may contain arbitrary NaNs; screening extra storage is a conservative rejection only.
findings.action: Tie the screen to getD or prove exact bounds before uget. A missing A read paired with Inf creates C through 0*Inf.

findings.claim: The mathematical closure theorem has no n<USize.size restriction. A USize implementation must preserve count and every address calculation, including baseB+k*p; count safety alone is insufficient.
findings.counterexample: If n=USize.size is blindly converted, count.toNat=0. A virtual input whose first word is 0x7fc00001 and remaining words zero makes a zero-length scan incorrectly accept the full NaN fold.
findings.action: Preserve existing Nat fallback for n>=USize.size and prove no-wrap address bounds, or implement the screen with Nat/getD. The virtual boundary example was not allocated or executed.

findings.claim: Allowing arbitrary qNaN or sNaN input words defeats a universal canonical-output guarantee, even for one element. Allowing only C is compatible with P and is not a counterexample.
findings.action: Keep the raw-nonNaN predicate, or explicitly prove a stronger P-based allowance; do not generalize from isSNaN=false alone.

findings.claim: Empty sum/dot is posZero and its native endpoint is nonNaN; the NaN antecedent is essential. Signed zero and subnormal cancellation remain nonNaN values and need no extra exclusion.
findings.action: Do not return C solely because an all-input screen is vacuously true. No n>0 hypothesis is needed if the endpoint-NaN condition is retained.

findings.claim: The supported FloatLib ofFloat32 path uses Float32.toBits. Fixed Lean toBits normalizes every runtime NaN to literal 0x7fc00000; header add/mul themselves are bare C arithmetic.
findings.action: Keep the existing ofFloat32/toBits conversion or construct the raw C word with its codec proof. Do not assume a raw hardware NaN bit-cast has the canonical sign/payload. New generated C/asm and runtime execution remain NOT_RUN.

findings.claim: W05 all-input toFloat32 homomorphism transports classification but has many raw NaN preimages. M21 nonNaN roundtrip cannot be applied at a NaN endpoint; M22 quiet absorption preserves an arbitrary quiet payload and does not make it canonical.
findings.action: First prove P of the exact raw fold. Then native endpoint NaN plus the forward projection forces its P alternative to be raw C. Do not invert toFloat32 on arbitrary raw words.
